review.plain: Fortune telling is claiming or pretending to tell fortunes, or claiming occult powers to answer questions, give advice or affect evil spirits or curses, for a fee; it is a class B misdemeanor.
acts: claims or pretends to tell fortunes
holds himself out as being able, by claimed or pretended use of occult powers, to answer questions or give advice on personal matters or to exorcise, influence or affect evil spirits or curses

penalties.penalty: Class B misdemeanor (sentence set in Penal Law Articles 70 and 80)

crimes.act: Claims or pretends to tell fortunes
ways: Holds himself out as being able, by claimed or pretended use of occult powers, to answer questions or give advice on personal matters or to exorcise, influence or affect evil spirits or curses
conditions: For a fee or compensation which he directly or indirectly solicits or receives
exceptions: This section does not apply to a person who engages in the aforedescribed conduct as part of a show or exhibition solely for the purpose of entertainment or amusement

review.plain: Criminal possession of stolen property in the fifth degree is knowingly possessing stolen property with intent to benefit oneself or another non-owner or to impede recovery by an owner; it is a class A misdemeanor.

intent: With intent to benefit himself or a person other than an owner thereof or to impede the recovery by an owner thereof

penalties.penalty: Class A misdemeanor (sentence set in Penal Law Articles 70 and 80)

review.plain: Criminal possession of stolen property in the fourth degree is knowingly possessing stolen property over $1,000, certain cards, firearms, motor vehicles, religious items or ammonia, or as a dealer; it is a class E felony.

intent: With intent to benefit himself or a person other than an owner thereof or to impede the recovery by an owner thereof

penalties.penalty: Class E felony (sentence set in Penal Law Article 70)

conditions: The value of the property exceeds one thousand dollars
The property consists of a credit card, debit card or public benefit card

crimes.who: A collateral loan broker or a person in the business of buying, selling or otherwise dealing in property

conditions: The property consists of one or more firearms, rifles and shotguns, as such terms are defined in section 265.00 of this chapter
The value of the property exceeds one hundred dollars

The property consists of a motor vehicle, as defined in section one hundred twenty-five of the vehicle and traffic law, other than a motorcycle, as defined in section one hundred twenty-three of such law

The property consists of a scroll, religious vestment, vessel or other item of property having a value of at least one hundred dollars kept for or used in connection with religious worship in any building or structure used as a place of religious worship by a religious corporation, as incorporated under the religious corporations law or the education law
The property consists of anhydrous ammonia or liquified ammonia gas
The actor intends to use, or knows another person intends to use, such anhydrous ammonia or liquified ammonia gas to manufacture methamphetamine

review.plain: Criminal possession of stolen property in the third degree is knowingly possessing stolen property worth more than $3,000, with intent to benefit a non-owner or impede recovery; it is a class D felony.

intent: With intent to benefit himself or a person other than an owner thereof or to impede the recovery by an owner thereof

penalties.penalty: Class D felony (sentence set in Penal Law Article 70)

conditions: The value of the property exceeds three thousand dollars

review.plain: Criminal possession of stolen property in the second degree is knowingly possessing stolen property worth more than $50,000, with intent to benefit a non-owner or impede recovery; it is a class C felony.

intent: With intent to benefit himself or a person other than an owner thereof or to impede the recovery by an owner thereof

penalties.penalty: Class C felony (sentence set in Penal Law Article 70)

conditions: The value of the property exceeds fifty thousand dollars

review.plain: Criminal possession of stolen property in the first degree is knowingly possessing stolen property worth more than $1 million, with intent to benefit a non-owner or impede recovery; it is a class B felony.

intent: With intent to benefit himself or a person other than an owner thereof or to impede the recovery by an owner

penalties.penalty: Class B felony (sentence set in Penal Law Article 70)

conditions: The value of the property exceeds one million dollars

review.plain: Sets presumptions for criminal possession of stolen property: of intent to benefit or impede recovery, and of knowledge that property was stolen for dealers and possessors of multiple stolen cards or air tickets; it creates no crime.

Says it is no defense to criminal possession of stolen property that the thief was not caught, that the defendant stole the property, or that the larceny occurred outside the state; it creates no crime.

Sets corroboration rules for convicting a person of criminal possession of stolen property on accomplice testimony or the testimony of those he obtained it from or disposed of it to; it creates no crime.
Fostering the sale of stolen goods is using a website, platform or location to offer for sale retail goods one knew or should have known were stolen, for financial gain; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: Uses any internet website, application, online marketplace, digital service, or any other platform or venue, including any physical building, public or private space, or location to offer for sale retail goods or merchandise which are stolen or unlawfully obtained

knowledge: Knew or should have known that such retail goods or merchandise were stolen or unlawfully obtained
intent: For the purposes of financial gain

penalties.penalty: Class A misdemeanor (sentence set in Penal Law Articles 70 and 80)

crimes.act: Uses any internet website, application, online marketplace, digital service, or any other platform or venue, including any physical building, public or private space, or location to offer for sale retail goods or merchandise which are stolen or unlawfully obtained
conditions: Acting alone or in concert with another person or persons

review.plain: Defines "trademark", "counterfeit trademark", "traffic" and "goods" for the trademark counterfeiting sections 165.71 through 165.74; it creates no crime.

Trademark counterfeiting in the third degree is making, distributing or selling goods bearing a counterfeit trademark, or possessing a counterfeit trademark to affix to goods, to deceive or defraud; it is a class a misdemeanor.
acts: manufactures, distributes, sells, or offers for sale goods which bear a counterfeit trademark

intent: With the intent to deceive or defraud some other person or with the intent to evade a lawful restriction on the sale, resale, offering for sale, or distribution of goods

penalties.penalty: Class A misdemeanor (sentence set in Penal Law Articles 70 and 80)

crimes.act: Manufactures, distributes, sells, or offers for sale goods which bear a counterfeit trademark

intent: With the intent to deceive or defraud some other person or with the intent to evade a lawful restriction on the sale, resale, offering for sale, or distribution of goods
For the purpose of affixing it to any goods
